transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve been having a lot of trouble focusing lately and keep making careless mistakes because I miss small details. I also feel constantly restless, like I’m always on the go and can't seem to slow down.
Do you also often interrupt others, blurt out answers before questions are finished, or have trouble waiting your turn?
I definitely struggle a lot with waiting my turn. It is really hard for me to wait in lines, and I find it very difficult to wait for my turn to speak during conversations or activities.
Do you also often lose things, forget appointments or daily tasks, or have trouble staying organized and finishing tasks?

Yes, I'm constantly losing important items like my keys, wallet, and work documents, which makes staying organized incredibly difficult. It is so frustrating because this happens almost daily and leads to so many careless mistakes on my tasks. I feel like I'm always wasting time searching for things I've misplaced.
Have these attention and restlessness symptoms been present since childhood, before age 12, and have they been causing problems in more than one setting like home, work, or school?

Yes, these issues definitely started during childhood, well before I was 12, and they've been actively causing me major problems for at least the last two years and two months. It affects almost every part of my life, especially at home with my family and at my job.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), and the interview further supports it rather than ruling it out. The patient endorses inattention (careless mistakes, losing items, disorganization, difficulty sustaining focus) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty waiting turn), with onset in childhood and impairment in multiple settings. No evidence emerged for an alternative diagnosis from the allowed list, so the candidate list remains unchanged.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear longstanding symptoms of both inattention (careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining focus, losing items, disorganization) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (restlessness, difficulty waiting turn, trouble waiting to speak), with onset in childhood and impairment in multiple settings (home and work), which supports ADHD, combined presentation.
